# `tabs/codec`

`serializeTabsLayout` stamps a version into the payload; `parseTabsLayout` reads one
back and never throws — unreadable input falls back, and a version it does not know is offered to
`migrate` first. Unparseable is a state, not an exception.

## Example

```ts
import { serializeTabsLayout, type TabsState, type WorkspaceSetup } from 'lightweight-magic-charts';

declare const state: TabsState<WorkspaceSetup>;

export const payload: string = serializeTabsLayout(state, 2);
```

## Exports

- **`coerceIndicatorList`** · value · `(raw: unknown, legacy: unknown, laneCount: number) => string[]`
- **`parseTabsLayout`** · value · `<S>(payload: string | null, options: TabsCodecOptions<S>) => TabsState<S>`
- **`serializeTabsLayout`** · value · `<S>(state: TabsState<S>, version: number) => string`
- **`TabsCodecOptions`** · type · `interface TabsCodecOptions { version: number; coerceSetup: (raw: unknown) => S; defaultName: (index: number) => string; seed: () => TabsState<S>; fallback: () => TabsState<S>; migrate?: ((record: Record<string, unknown>) => TabsState<S> | null) | undefined }`
